name: Ectodermal Dysplasia-Hyperhidrosis-Cutaneous Syndactyly Syndrome
aliases: Ectodermal Dysplasia with Hyperhidrosis and Cutaneous Syndactyly

criteria.description: Presence of ectodermal dysplasia features including abnormal hair, teeth, and nails
Generalized or localized excessive sweating beyond physiological needs
Cutaneous syndactyly involving fusion of digits without bony involvement
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Exclusion of other syndromes with overlapping features such as Clouston syndrome or other ectodermal dysplasias

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: ectodermal dysplasia features, hyperhidrosis, and cutaneous syndactyly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not always available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous syndactyly of fingers or toes
pathognomonic.notes: Typically involves soft tissue fusion without bone involvement
Excessive sweating often present from infancy or early childhood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypotrichosis with sparse, thin scalp hair
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic hair abnormalities consistent with ectodermal dysplasia

common.notes: Missing teeth or abnormal tooth development
Thickened, brittle, or abnormally shaped nails
Generalized skin dryness common in ectodermal dysplasias

common.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia
common.notes: Subtle craniofacial abnormalities may be present
searchTerms: unusual facial features with prominent forehead and flat midface

occasional.notes: Due to impaired thermoregulation from hyperhidrosis
Reported in some cases but not consistent
Thickening of skin on palms and soles

rare.notes: Occasional susceptibility possibly related to ectodermal abnormalities

laboratory: Possible mild electrolyte imbalance due to excessive sweating
imaging: X-rays showing soft tissue syndactyly without bony fusion
genetic: Mutations in genes related to ectodermal development (specific gene not yet identified)
Inheritance pattern may be autosomal dominant or recessive
other: Clinical observation of hyperhidrosis and syndactyly
Family history consistent with ectodermal dysplasia spectrum disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of nail dystrophy and palmoplantar keratoderma without syndactyly
Characteristic nail and hair abnormalities with normal sweating
Presence of lacrimal duct anomalies and dental abnormalities
Syndactyly less common and hyperhidrosis absent

redFlags: Excessive hyperhidrosis leading to dehydration or electrolyte imbalance
Early onset developmental delay or neurological symptoms
references: Orphanet: Ectodermal Dysplasia-Hyperhidrosis-Cutaneous Syndactyly Syndrome, ORPHA:247827
Pinheiro M, Freire-Maia N. Ectodermal dysplasias: a clinical classification and a causal review. Am J Med Genet. 1994;53(2):153-162.
Clarke A, et al. Syndactyly and ectodermal dysplasia: clinical and genetic aspects. Eur J Dermatol. 2018;28(3):345-352.
